chunks: Is'haq, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Aqraʿ, who said: Abū Ḥamzah Nuṣayr al-Khādim narrated to me, saying:

I heard Abū Muḥammad more than once speaking to his servants in their own languages: Turkish, Roman, and Saqālibah. So I was amazed at that and said: This one was born in al-Madīnah, and he did not appear to anyone until Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام passed away, and no one had seen him, so how is this?

I was speaking to myself about that, when he turned toward me and said: Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, distinguishes His proof from the rest of His creation by means of everything, and He gives him the languages, knowledge of lineages, lifespans, and events. Were it not for that, there would be no difference between the divine proof and the one over whom the proof is established.

key_terms.اللُّغَاتِ: the various languages granted to the Imam as a sign of divinely bestowed knowledge
key_terms.الْآجَالِ: appointed lifespans or terms of death
key_terms.الْمَحْجُوجِ: the one over whom the proof is established, in contrast to the divine proof
key_terms.حُجَّتَهُ: His divine proof, meaning the Imam as Allah’s authoritative proof over creation

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the signs that distinguish Allah’s hujjah from other people?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a sign of the Imam’s divinely granted knowledge, shown through his ability to speak multiple languages and know matters beyond ordinary acquisition. It explains that Allah distinguishes His hujjah from the rest of creation through special knowledge and capacities, which serve as marks of religious authority.

en.hubeali: Is’haq, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Al Aqra’a who said, ‘Abu Hamza Nuseyr al Khadim narrated to me saying,

‘I heard Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> more than once speaking to his<sup>asws</sup> servants in their own language, Turkish, or Roman, and Saqaliba. So I was astonished from that and I said, ‘This (Imam<sup>asws</sup>) is born in Al-Medina and he<sup>asws</sup> did not appear to anyone until Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> passed away, and no one saw him<sup>asws</sup>, so how can this be?’

I was discussing that with myself and he<sup>asws</sup> turned towards me, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High Clarified His<sup>azwj</sup> Divine Authority from the rest of the people with everything, and He<sup>azwj</sup> Gave him the languages and the recognition of the lineages, and the terms (of death), and the occurrences, and had it not been for that, there would not have been a difference between the Divine Authority and others (entities)’.
